name: Question 2
problem: The second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)={e}^{\pi x/2}$ about $x=0$ is
worked_solution:
To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=0,$ we plug $a=0$ into the general formula to give

$$
{P}_{2}(x)=f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)(x-0)+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(0)(x-0)^{2}.
$$

So, we need to work out $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ and ${f}^{″}(0):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={e}^{\pi x/2} & ⟹ &  & f(0) & =1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\pi }{2}{e}^{\pi x/2} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(0) & =\frac{\pi }{2} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}{e}^{\pi x/2} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(0) & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We now plug the results for $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ and ${f}^{″}(0)$ into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =1+(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot x+(\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4})\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{2} \\  & =1+\frac{\pi }{2}x+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{8}{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

The second-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x)=eπx/2 about x=0 is

a
1−π2x2+π28x4
b
1+π2x+π28x2
c
x+π2x2+π36x3
d
1+π2x+π24x2
e
π−π22x−3π38x2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about x=0, we plug a=0 into the general formula to give

P2(x)=f(0)+f′(0)(x−0)+12f″(0)(x−0)2.

So, we need to work out f(0), f′(0), and f″(0):

f(x)=eπx/2⟹f(0)=1f′(x)=π2eπx/2⟹f′(0)=π2f″(x)=π24eπx/2⟹f″(0)=π24

We now plug the results for f(0), f′(0), and f″(0) into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

P2(x)=1+(π2)⋅x+(π24)⋅12x2=1+π2x+π28x2.
